assessment.summary: Cross-cutting C++20 practice sweep over engine/include, engine/src and tools (exempt comp-strategy headers skipped). The DSP core is consistently structured: a self-describing ValueSource API built on std::span/std::string_view descriptor tables, enum class and final on leaf nodes, std::variant for articulations, RAII scope guards, no raw new/delete anywhere in engine/, atomics for cross-thread state and off-thread voice destruction in the UI. The dominant problem is that the project's own real-time rule (no heap, locks or unbounded work in per-sample paths) is broken in several engine render paths independent of the UI: WaveSource::next() throws with no exception boundary on the audio thread (a throw the perform_source.h comment confirms has fired), WavetableSource/HybridKS/BasicAdditive and four WaveEvolution subclasses allocate inside next()/evolve(), RepeatingSource::next() re-runs prepare() on arbitrary subgraphs, and the UI audio callback blocks on a mutex the UI thread holds across graph rebuilds. The second-order problem is boilerplate volume: descriptor names are hand-repeated across descriptors/set_param/get_param if-chains (with one documented default-drift bug), a macro splices descriptor rows, JSON walkers/voice-pool builds/stereo-write blocks/filter sections are copy-pasted, and mforce_ui/main.cpp is a 14,658-line file with 349 file-scope statics and three parallel node serializers. Modern-C++ hygiene gaps are broad but cheap: zero [[nodiscard]] and zero noexcept across the tree, 39 duplicated PI literals, unscoped enums and non-explicit single-argument constructors, namespace-scope using-aliases in headers, uninitialized aggregate members including a null-dereferencing Pitch{} sentinel, const_cast on const PieceTemplate& in the composer, and a thread_local ambient RNG with no null check.
strengths: Descriptor API uses std::span + std::string_view (ParamDescriptor/InputDescriptor/SettingDescriptor/ArrayDescriptor) and static constexpr tables; enum class + final on leaf ValueSource types
No raw new/delete or malloc in engine/ (only four `new` sites in composer.h, all immediately wrapped); std::variant for articulations/ornaments; std::optional used for template fields
RAII scopes (TapBindScope, rng::Scope) and std::atomic for InstrumentState / audio-restart flags; UI voice_gc() releases DSP graphs off the audio thread
Documented fast_math (fast_sin_turns/fast_exp2), denormal flushing enabled at process start, double-precision PierceAllpass state and double-precision sin in FMSource for the spacy-FM reproduction
RefSource advancer model and guarded taps give a clear ownership/advance contract for feedback loops; tap guard is unit-tested (engine_tests run_tap_guard_tests / run_tap_cycle_tests)
Assertion-style engine_tests covers RT-relevant semantics (phase delay, loop compensation, passivity gate for PierceFilter) rather than only render-based checks

UI copy/paste rides the real saver/loader so the fragment format cannot drift from the file format; headless CLI modes (--roundtrip, --gencheck, --dump-playback) make UI behaviour verifiable from a terminal

findings.title: WaveSource::next() throws on the render thread and the UI audio callback has no exception boundary
findings.evidence: if (f <= 0.0f) throw std::runtime_error("WaveSource: non-positive frequency");  // inside per-sample next(); tools/mforce_ui/main.cpp:3890 `float vs = voice.source->next() * voice.gain;` with no try/catch anywhere in audio_callback (3857-3999)
findings.why: An exception escaping an RtAudio callback thread calls std::terminate and kills the whole UI process. perform_source.h:117 documents that exactly this throw has already fired in practice ("That surfaced as 'WaveSource: non-positive..."). wavetable_source.cpp:23 (`throw std::runtime_error("WavetableSource: invalid frequency for table fill")`, reached from compute_raw via fill_table at line 46) has the same shape.
findings.recommendation: Never throw from next()/prepare(): clamp or substitute (return 0 and set a sticky error flag the UI/CLI can report). Validate frequency inputs at wiring/set_param time instead. As a defence in depth, wrap the body of audio_callback in try/catch that zero-fills the buffer and sets an atomic error flag.

findings.title: Audio callback blocks on g_audioMutex that the UI thread holds across graph rebuilds and voice preparation
findings.evidence: 3864: `std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_audioMutex);` in audio_callback; 1023: update_all_dsp() takes the same lock and builds RefSources/unordered_maps; 4676-4693: play_note() holds it across collect_envelopes(...) and pitched->prepare_voice_at(...)
findings.why: A std::mutex in the audio thread is priority inversion by construction: any UI-side rebuild (JSON-driven MultiplexSource::rebuild_, Vibrato::build_lfo allocation, dynamic_cast walks in DelayLineSource::prepare) stalls the callback for its full duration, producing dropouts. The 26 lock sites (grep count) show the mutex is the only synchronization primitive between the two threads.
findings.recommendation: Replace the mutex with a lock-free handoff: build voices/graphs fully on the UI thread, publish them through an SPSC command queue or atomic pointer swap, and have the callback only consume ready-to-run state; retire graphs through the existing voice_gc path. Use try_lock as an interim mitigation (skip the block rather than wait).

findings.title: Table allocation deferred to the first next(): WavetableSource, HybridKSSource and BasicAdditiveSource resize vectors inside the sample path
findings.evidence: 27: `values_.resize(len);` in fill_table(), called at 46 from compute_raw (first next()); engine/src/hybrid_ks_source.cpp:35 `table_.resize(len);` and 52-54 `partialAmpl_.resize(numPartials_); partialPhase_.resize(...); startAmpl_.resize(...)`; engine/include/mforce/source/additive/basic_additive_source.h:121 `partialPos_.resize(count, 0.0f);` inside compute_wave_value
findings.why: These are heap allocations on the render thread, violating the project's hot-loop rule. In the UI they run under the audio mutex at note-on; in RepeatingSource-driven graphs they recur every repetition.
findings.recommendation: Size tables in prepare() (or at set_param time when the frequency is known) and treat next() as allocation-free; assert capacity in debug builds.

findings.title: WaveEvolution::evolve() implementations allocate per table cycle (HistogramEqualize, TargetEvolution, BezierPull, CellularAutomaton)
findings.evidence: 1328: `std::vector<int> counts(bins, 0);` in rebuild_cdf(), called from evolve at 1310 `if (index == 0) rebuild_cdf(values);` i.e. every cycle; 195: `resampledTarget_.resize(len);` (TargetEvolution::evolve 189); 1407: `target_.resize(len);` (BezierPull evolve 1398); 1216-1217: `state_.assign(len, 0); snapshot_.assign(len, 0);` (CellularAutomaton evolve 1211)
findings.why: evolve() is invoked per sample from WavetableSource::compute_raw (wavetable_source.cpp:69 `evolution_->evolve(values_, tablePtr2_)` and 127); a fresh std::vector<int> per fundamental period is a steady-state allocation on the audio thread, not a one-off.
findings.recommendation: Make counts a member sized in prepare() (std::vector<int> counts_ reused with std::fill), and move all len-dependent resizes to a `void prepare(int len)` hook on WaveEvolution called by WavetableSource::prepare.

findings.title: RepeatingSource::next() re-runs prepare() on its subgraph, pulling unbounded setup work (JSON graph rebuilds, node allocation, RTTI walks) into the sample path
findings.evidence: 95: `prepare_repetition();` inside next(); 112: `if (source_) source_->prepare(ctx_, samples);`. Subgraph prepare() is not bounded: multiplex_source.h:106 `if (templateDirty_) rebuild_();` (134-151 constructs count_ clone graphs via std::function builder_), vibrato.h:98 `build_lfo();` (121 allocates the LFO node chain), delay_line_source.h:154 `if (auto* rs = dynamic_cast<RefSource*>(n))` walk; delay_line_source.h:90 even states "prepare() may run at note-on in the audio callback"
findings.why: prepare() is the one place the engine allows allocation; calling it from next() makes every node's prepare cost a per-sample cost at repetition boundaries, and does so on the audio thread in the UI.
findings.recommendation: Give ValueSource a cheap `reset()`/`retrigger()` (state-only, no allocation) and have RepeatingSource call that; keep prepare() strictly for load/setup. MultiplexSource must rebuild from set_setting/set_array, never lazily in prepare().

findings.title: render_chunk resizes the output vector per call and is called with n=1 per sample; its 'caller must reserve' contract is only honoured for the first note of a line
findings.evidence: 442: `buf.resize(base + size_t(n));`; 631 and 686: `render_chunk(vg, buf, vIdx, startFrame, 1, gain);` / `render_chunk(vg, buf, line_.vIdx, startFrame, 1, line_.gain);`; contract at 436-437 "buf must be reserved by the caller: the resize below then allocates nothing" but the only reserve is 590-591 `line_.buf.reserve(size_t(durSamples + int(kMaxRingSec * float(sampleRate))));` sized for the first note's duration
findings.why: A held line whose later notes extend past the first note's reserved capacity reallocates line_.buf (copying the whole line) in the middle of per-sample rendering, on whichever thread drives the instrument (the UI's live path).
findings.recommendation: Reserve for the line's maximum (or grow in prepare/at note-on outside the per-sample loop), or give render_chunk a span/pointer target with the caller responsible for capacity, and assert `buf.capacity() >= base + n` in debug.

findings.title: Mixer::render allocates a scratch vector on every block
findings.evidence: std::vector<float> mono(frames);
findings.why: Per-block heap allocation in a render path; today Mixer::render is only reached from the offline CLI (the UI mixes node graphs itself at main.cpp:3966), so the practical cost is allocator churn rather than dropouts, but it blocks ever reusing the engine mixer live.
findings.recommendation: Keep a member scratch buffer sized in a prepare()/set_block_size step, or render channels directly into the interleaved output.

findings.title: compose(const PieceTemplate&) mutates the template through const_cast
findings.evidence: 405: `::mforce::realize_motifs(const_cast<PieceTemplate&>(tmpl), rng_);`; 820: `Locus locus{&piece, const_cast<PieceTemplate*>(&tmpl), 0, 0};`; 859: same for per-section loci; 879-881: `const_cast<Section*>(section)->harmonyTimeline.set_segment(` / `->chordProgression = prog;`
findings.why: Modifying an object through a pointer obtained by casting away constness is undefined behaviour when the original object is const (a caller holding a `const PieceTemplate` literal or a template shared between threads). The signature promises non-mutation that strategies rely on being false (they write realizedMotifs and section harmony).
findings.recommendation: Take `PieceTemplate&` (or by value) in compose(), or split the mutable realization state (realizedMotifs, section harmony) into a separate CompositionState owned by the composer and referenced from Locus.

findings.title: Ambient thread_local RNG dereferenced without a null check; public strategy dispatchers can run without a Scope installed
findings.evidence: 8: `inline thread_local Randomizer* current = nullptr;`  11: `inline uint32_t next() { return detail::current->rng(); }`; composer.h public dispatchers at 241-254 invoke strategies directly without installing rng::Scope
findings.why: Any strategy that calls mforce::rng::next() outside a Scope null-dereferences; hidden thread-local state also makes seed reproducibility (a project non-negotiable) depend on call-order rather than data.
findings.recommendation: Assert/throw on null in next(), and pass the Randomizer explicitly through Locus or the strategy interface instead of an ambient global.

findings.title: Function-local static Randomizer shared by all builders breaks per-seed reproducibility and is a data race across composers
findings.evidence: static Randomizer countRng(0x0C117u);
findings.why: The count draw advances a process-wide stream, so two compositions with identical masterSeed produce different figures depending on what ran before; two composers on different threads race on it. Contradicts the seeds-in-JSON reproducibility rule.
findings.recommendation: Draw from the builder's own seeded Randomizer (already a member) or from the Locus/strategy RNG.

findings.title: Uninitialized aggregate members: Pitch{} is a null-pointer sentinel that note_number() dereferences; Chord::def, Section::beats and PoolAtom fields are likewise uninitialized
findings.evidence: 116-117: `const PitchDef* pitchDef;` / `int octave;` then 119: `float note_number() const { return float(octave * 12 + pitchDef->offset); }`; piece_utils.h:38,39,46,92 `return Pitch{};`; basics.h:335 `const ChordDef* def;`; structure.h:198 `float beats;` not set by the default ctor at 209 `Section() : scale(Scale::get("C", "Major")) {}`; pool_figure_builder.h:17-20 `int noteCount; float totalBeats; Contour contour; long count;`
findings.why: A default-constructed Pitch/Chord/Section has indeterminate or null members; any consumer of the piece_utils sentinel that calls note_number() crashes, and a default Section carries garbage beats into timing math.
findings.recommendation: Add default member initializers (`const PitchDef* pitchDef{nullptr}; int octave{4};`, `float beats{0.0f};`), return std::optional<Pitch> from the lookup helpers instead of a sentinel, and make note_number() precondition-checked.

findings.title: Exceptions used as control flow inside complexify; smooth_voicing_selector swallows everything with catch(...)
findings.evidence: 372: `try {` ... 376: `} catch (const std::invalid_argument&) {` steering the transform retry path; smooth_voicing_selector.h:46 `} catch (...) {`
findings.why: Throw/catch in a per-figure generation loop costs microseconds per iteration and hides which precondition failed; catch(...) in the voicing selector masks real bugs (including bad_alloc) as 'no voicing'.
findings.recommendation: Return std::optional/expected from the inner helper and branch on it; narrow the catch in smooth_voicing_selector to the specific exception type and log it.

findings.title: const member mutates through const_cast instead of a mutable cache
findings.evidence: if (arrayUpdateReq_) const_cast<Partials*>(this)->update_arrays();
findings.why: A const accessor that rewrites member arrays is a hidden write; the codebase has zero `mutable` members, so the lazy-cache idiom is expressed by casting rather than by type. Calling it on a genuinely const Partials is UB.
findings.recommendation: Declare the lazily-rebuilt arrays and the flag `mutable`, or make get_array non-const.

findings.title: Macro splices shared descriptor rows into four descriptor tables; descriptor names are otherwise hand-triplicated across descriptors/set_param/get_param with a documented drift bug
findings.evidence: 175: `#define MFORCE_PARTIALS_MOTION_CONFIG_DESCS \` used at 314, 1094, 1196, 1277; range_source.h:77-80 comment: "Default FALSE to match the loader's absent-key contract ... It was 1.0 here, so the UI displayed true for patches that omit the key and wrote true back on save — audibly changing them"
findings.why: Every node repeats its parameter names as string literals in the descriptor table, in set_param/get_param/set_setting/get_setting if-chains and in the loader; the RangeSource bug is the measured cost of that triplication. A macro is the only reuse mechanism in use.
findings.recommendation: Replace the macro with a constexpr std::array base table and a constexpr concat helper (or std::span over a shared static array), and drive set/get dispatch from the descriptor table (index lookup + pointer-to-member) so a name exists exactly once per node.

findings.title: loadPhrase lambda re-implements from_json(PhraseTemplate); connector parsing is verbatim in both
findings.evidence: 799: `auto loadPhrase = [](const json& pj) {` duplicates 692 `inline void from_json(const json& j, PhraseTemplate& pt)`; connector block 741-758 (`if (j.contains("connectors")) { pt.connectors.clear(); for (const auto& cj : j.at("connectors")) { if (cj.is_null()) ...`) is identical to 821-838 modulo `pt`/`ph` and `j`/`pj`; the justification comment at 797 ("does not use from_json(PhraseTemplate) directly (which enforces startingPitch)") describes an enforcement not present in 692-759
findings.why: Two parsers for one schema drift independently (new PhraseTemplate fields must be added twice); the stated reason for the second copy does not match the code.
findings.recommendation: Delete loadPhrase and call from_json; if period phrases genuinely need a relaxed startingPitch rule, express it as a parameter/flag on the single parser.

findings.title: Recursive JSON ref/tap walker copied three times and the voice-pool build copied twice ('see render-path twin above')
findings.evidence: 190: `std::function<void(const json&)> scan = [&](const json& v) {` with the same body at 235 (`scanRefs`) and 1104 (`scanRefs`), plus scanIds at 206 and 247; voice-pool construction 1534-1540 `for (int v = 0; v < polyphony; ++v) { PitchedInstrument::VoiceGraph vg; PerformContext perf = make_perform_context(...); auto g = build_graph(...)` repeated at 1855-1860, with comments at 1868/1880/1882 "see render-path twin above"
findings.why: The tap/ref scanning rules (which decide advancer ownership and starved-ref promotion) are soundness-critical; three copies mean a fix to one silently misses the others. The two voice-pool builders already differ (render vs live) only in surroundings, and the comments admit the duplication.
findings.recommendation: Factor `for_each_ref(const json&, callback)` (a plain recursive function, no std::function) and a `build_voice_pool(nodeMap, nodeOrder, sampleRate, inst, polyphony)` helper used by both paths.

findings.title: Mono-to-stereo interleave + write_wav_16le_stereo block duplicated seven times
findings.evidence: 106 `stereo[i * 2]     = mono[i];` + 110 `if (!write_wav_16le_stereo(outPath, ip.sampleRate, stereo))`; same block at 187/191, 327/331, 618/623, 722/726, 886-892, 1006/1010
findings.why: Peak/RMS reporting and output-path handling drift between subcommands; one change (e.g. dithering or 24-bit) has to land in seven places.
findings.recommendation: Add `write_mono_as_stereo_wav(path, sr, span<const float>)` (and a peak/rms helper) in wav_writer and call it from each subcommand.

findings.title: Butterworth LP/HP sections and filters are near-identical copies; BiquadState + ap1_phase_delay duplicated between KSString and AllpassResonator
findings.evidence: 54 `struct BWLPSection {` vs 85 `struct BWHPSection {` differing only in omegac (67 `2.0 * rate * std::tan(...)` vs 98 `1.0 / (2.0 * rate * std::tan(...))`) and BWLowpassFilter/BWHighpassFilter likewise; ks_string.h:394 `struct BiquadState { float x1{0}, x2{0}, y1{0}, y2{0}; };` and 438 `static float ap1_phase_delay(float a, float w)` reappear verbatim at allpass_resonator.h:176 and 178
findings.why: Filter coefficient math is where sign/scaling bugs live; two copies double the audit surface and the phase-delay helper is loop-tuning-critical (used in loop compensation).
findings.recommendation: Template the section on a Kind enum (or pass the omegac transform as a lambda) and move BiquadState/ap1_phase_delay to a shared filter header.

findings.title: 14,658-line single translation unit with 349 file-scope statics and three parallel node serializers plus two clipboard systems
findings.evidence: serialize_patch_graph 2806 and save_node_graph 3275 emit the same per-node blocks (3028 `jnode["params"]["stages"] = envelope_stages_to_json(*env);` / 3068 formants / 3101 seed vs 3349 / 3380 / 3411); clip_node_state 10286-10331 is a third serializer; s_clipboard (10276, in-process JSON) and copy_selection_to_clipboard (11273, OS clipboard fragment) are two independent copy/paste implementations wired to different menus (Edit menu 13738-13743 vs context menu 11542 / Ctrl+C 14255); eval_map_curve 4484 mirrors engine curve evaluation
findings.why: Node state has to be kept consistent in 3 serializers and 2 loaders; the duplicated clipboard paths already diverge in capability (one handles groups/positions, one skips Note/Output). The file size defeats incremental builds and review.
findings.recommendation: Split into graph_model (GraphNode/Link/groups + one serializer with a mode flag), audio_engine_bridge (callback, voice pool), editor (imnodes), panels; delete the s_clipboard path in favour of the saver-backed fragment path; have the UI call the engine's Curve::eval instead of mirroring it.

findings.title: Library code writes diagnostics straight to stderr/cerr (58 sites in engine/)
findings.evidence: 306 `std::fprintf(stderr, "[onset] name '%s' is not in this "`, also 553, 651, 700; patch_loader.cpp 12 fprintf(stderr) sites; composer.h:250, 260, 637, 654, 1586, 1631, 1633, 2041 `std::cerr << ...`
findings.why: mforce_ui is a WIN32-subsystem app where stderr is swallowed (its own crash-log comment at 12781-12783 says so), so engine warnings about unknown onsets, dropped bindings and fallback strategies are invisible exactly where patches are edited; fprintf is also not RT-safe (instrument.h:553/651/700 sit in note-on paths).
findings.recommendation: Route through a `mforce::log(Level, string_view)` sink with a settable callback (default: stderr in CLI, status bar/crash log in UI), and make RT-path warnings set a flag that is reported off-thread.

findings.title: Transitive-include reliance and unused includes
findings.evidence: 398: `std::strlen(desc.enum_labels[li])` plus std::tolower/std::equal/std::sin/std::lround used with includes 33-40 limited to `<nlohmann/json.hpp> <fstream> <functional> <cstdio> <sstream> <stdexcept> <unordered_map> <unordered_set>` (no <cstring>, <cctype>, <algorithm>, <cmath>); conductor.h:393 `snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%g", chord.dur);` and parse_util.h:158 without <cstdio>; unused: red_noise_source.cpp:4 `#include <iostream>`, dun_parser.h:11 `#include <iostream>`, phased_value_source.h:9 `#include <stdexcept>`
findings.why: Compiles today only because nlohmann/json.hpp happens to pull those headers; an MSVC STL or nlohmann update breaks the build in files that look unrelated. <iostream> in a hot DSP .cpp adds static-init cost for nothing.
findings.recommendation: Include what you use (add the four headers to patch_loader.cpp, <cstdio> to conductor.h/parse_util.h); drop the unused includes; consider clang-tidy misc-include-cleaner in CI.

findings.title: Namespace-scope `using json = nlohmann::json;` in public headers
findings.evidence: music_json.h:13 `using json = nlohmann::json;`; templates_json.h:9 same; style_table.h:15 same (all inside namespace mforce)
findings.why: Every includer of mforce/music gets a global-looking `json` identifier injected into namespace mforce, which collides with any other json type and makes the dependency on nlohmann part of the public interface.
findings.recommendation: Qualify as nlohmann::json in headers (or a project-level `mforce::Json` alias in one deliberate header); keep `using json` to .cpp files.

findings.title: Unchecked float-to-enum conversion for the operation setting
findings.evidence: if (name == "operation") { op = static_cast<CombineOp>(int(value)); return; }
findings.why: Any out-of-range setting value (UI drag, hand-edited JSON) yields a CombineOp with no enumerator; the switch on it then falls to whatever default exists, silently changing the sound.
findings.recommendation: Clamp/validate against the enum_labels count from the descriptor before casting.

findings.title: Exact float equality on an accumulated beat cursor decides barline figure boundaries
findings.evidence: 110: `const float beatInBar = std::fmod(passageBeat, beatsPerBar);` 113: `} else if (beatInBar == 0.0f && !fig.units.empty()) {` with 128 `passageBeat += n.durationSeconds;`
findings.why: Durations that are not exactly representable (triplets 1/3, 2/3) accumulate rounding error, so a barline lands at 3.9999998 and the figure boundary is silently skipped, merging two figures.
findings.recommendation: Compare with a tolerance (`std::fabs(beatInBar) < 1e-4f || std::fabs(beatInBar - beatsPerBar) < 1e-4f`) or track beats in integer ticks.

findings.title: RTTI cross-casts in the wiring path
findings.evidence: formant.h:320 and 328 `auto fmt = std::dynamic_pointer_cast<IFormant>(src);`; additive_source2.h:82 `std::dynamic_pointer_cast<Partials>(src)`; full_additive_source.h:49, 56, 64, 67; delay_line_source.h:154 `if (auto* rs = dynamic_cast<RefSource*>(n))` inside prepare()
findings.why: set_param has to guess the concrete type behind a shared_ptr<ValueSource> because interface pins are not typed; the loader silently drops mismatches (the UI's pin_type_compat_error exists to paper over this). dynamic_cast in prepare() also runs on the note-on path.
findings.recommendation: Add typed setters (`set_formant(std::shared_ptr<IFormant>)`) declared in the descriptor (InputDescriptor already carries a kind) so the loader dispatches without RTTI; cache the RefSource walk result at load.

findings.title: Zero [[nodiscard]] and zero noexcept across engine and tools; move operations not noexcept so vector reallocation copies
findings.evidence: grep over engine/include, engine/src, tools: 0 occurrences of `[[nodiscard]]`, 0 of `noexcept` (excluding third_party); UI s_nodes is a std::vector<GraphNode> whose reallocation hazards are hand-annotated at 10580 ("node creation can reallocate s_nodes"), 10687, 11164
findings.why: Accessors like get_param/get_setting/next() can be called and discarded without a warning; without noexcept moves, std::vector growth of node-holding structs falls back to copy, and the UI already has three comments warning about pointer invalidation on emplace_back.
findings.recommendation: Mark pure accessors and factory functions [[nodiscard]]; declare move ctors/assignments `= default` noexcept on value types held in vectors (GraphNode, Pin, Link, FigureUnit); consider std::deque or index handles for s_nodes.

findings.title: 39 hand-typed PI literals instead of std::numbers
findings.evidence: filters.h:63 `std::cos(3.14159265358979 * (2.0 * k + n - 1.0) / (2.0 * n))`, also 67, 94, 98; mixer.cpp:41-42; svf_source.h:106, 119, 155; biquad_source.h:104, 130; envelope.h:522; hybrid_ks_source.cpp:7; basic_additive_source.h:135; tools/mforce_ui/main.cpp:3966-3967, 13383; stk_ref/mesh2d_ref.cpp:181 (39 total)
findings.why: Mixed precisions (`3.14159265358979` double in filters.h vs `3.14159265358979323846f` elsewhere) and local `constexpr float PI` redefinitions; C++20 provides std::numbers::pi_v<float>.
findings.recommendation: Replace with std::numbers::pi_v<float>/<double> (one include of <numbers>); keep TAU as a single constexpr in fast_math.h.

findings.title: Unscoped enums and non-explicit single-argument constructors
findings.evidence: svf_source.h:30 `enum Mode { kLowpass = 0, kHighpass = 1, kBandpass = 2, kLowpass1P = 3, kHighpass1P = 4 };`; partials.h:246 `enum PartialsRngLayer : uint32_t {`; biquad_source.h:20 `BiquadSource(int sampleRate)`; envelope_presets.h:30, 85, 143, 203, 263, 331 `AREnvelope(int sampleRate) : Envelope(sampleRate) ...`; partials.h:267 `Partials(uint32_t seed = 0xADD2'0000u)`, 1073, 1176, 1260
findings.why: Unscoped enums leak enumerators and convert to int implicitly (svf mode is already set from a float at test line 300); non-explicit ctors allow `std::shared_ptr<Partials> p = 48000;`-style accidental conversions and int-to-node conversions in overload resolution.
findings.recommendation: Use `enum class` (the rest of the codebase already does) and mark single-argument constructors `explicit`.

findings.title: C-style casts in music, tools and test harnesses
findings.evidence: parse_util.h:306 `if (pos < (int)token.size() && token[pos] == '#')`, 309, 320; chord_walker.h:117 `for (int i = 0; i < (int)attackBeats.size(); ++i)`, 119, 180, 249, 312; segment_source.h:250 `const long long target = (long long)std::llround(accExact);` (llround already returns long long); mforce_cli/main.cpp:773 `(size_t)p.frames`; build_stamp.h:112 `reinterpret_cast<const wchar_t*>(raw.data() + 2)`; stk_ref/*.cpp `(int16_t)std::lrint(s * 32767.0)`, `(uint32_t)samples.size()`
findings.why: C casts hide narrowing and pointer reinterpretation; the engine proper uses static_cast/functional casts consistently, so this is inconsistency rather than danger.
findings.recommendation: Use static_cast/std::ssize (C++20) for size comparisons; drop the redundant llround cast.

findings.title: Per-sample transcendental recomputation and non-const/double-evaluated helpers in sample paths
findings.evidence: limiter.h:90 `float releaseCoef = std::exp(-1.0f / std::max(1.0f, relSec * float(sampleRate_)));` inside the per-sample loop; shaper_source.h:206 `float map(float x) {` is non-const though it only reads; pulse_source.h:54-59 and basic_additive_source.h:97-111 evaluate the same sub-expression twice per sample
findings.why: std::exp per sample in a limiter that sits on every voice output is avoidable cost; a non-const map() prevents calling it from const contexts (the UI already works around this).
findings.recommendation: Cache releaseCoef when relSec changes (compare-and-update), make map() const, hoist the repeated sub-expressions.

findings.title: Public data members with private naming, and inconsistent constexpr-ness of descriptor tables
findings.evidence: envelope.h:44 `float timeScale_{1.0f};`, 53-54 `std::shared_ptr<ValueSource> minValue_; maxValue_;`, 159 `std::shared_ptr<ValueSource> trigger_;` all public; svf_source.h:56 `static const SettingDescriptor descs[] = {` while sibling tables at 38/46 are `static constexpr`
findings.why: Trailing-underscore names signal 'private' everywhere else in the engine; readers (and the UI, which pokes env->absolute_time directly at main.cpp:10036) cannot tell which fields are API. `static const` tables are initialised at first use rather than constant-initialised.
findings.recommendation: Either make them private with accessors or drop the underscore; make all descriptor tables constexpr.

findings.title: goto-based loop control in explore and unchecked atof/duplicated WAV writer across the stk_ref harnesses
findings.evidence: explore.cpp:324 `goto next_variant;`, 386, 391; stk_ref: `if (argc > 2) kSampleRate = atof(argv[2]);` in brass_ref.cpp:68, flute_ref.cpp:68, clarinet_ref.cpp:71, blowhole_ref.cpp:75, saxofony_ref.cpp:77, bandedwg_ref.cpp:73, bowed_ref.cpp:85, mesh2d_ref.cpp:263; `write_wav16_mono` copied verbatim in all eight (brass 24-46, flute 23-45, clarinet 26-48, blowhole 28-50, saxofony 28-50, bandedwg 28-50, bowed 31-55, mesh2d 192-213)
findings.why: atof returns 0 on garbage, which then sets Stk sample rate 0 and divides by zero in frame counts; the eight-way copy of the WAV writer is harness-only cost but any header-format fix has to be made eight times. goto in explore is readable but a `continue` in a lambda/for would be idiomatic.
findings.recommendation: Share a tiny stk_ref_common.h (WAV writer, midi_hz, argv parsing with std::from_chars validation); replace goto with a helper returning bool.
